title: Public endpoint returns every user with password hash
explanation: GET /api/auth/clients is under the permitAll rule for /api/auth/** and returns userRepository.findAll(): every User entity, including pwd (bcrypt hash), role, phone, birth date and the accountant code.
fix: Remove the endpoint or move it under /api/admin; never return entities, only DTOs without secrets.

title: Public lookup of any user by e-mail (enumeration + data exposure)
explanation: GET /api/auth/{email} is public and returns the full User entity (password hash, image, code). Its 404 message also confirms whether an e-mail exists.
fix: Delete it or restrict it to the authenticated user; return a minimal DTO.

title: Password hashes leak through DTOs that embed User entities
location: app/api/src/main/java/com/domiaffaire/api/entities/User.java:27; app/api/src/main/java/com/domiaffaire/api/dto/UserDTO.java:16; app/api/src/main/java/com/domiaffaire/api/dto/BlogDTO.java:16 (also ChatDTO, ConsultationRequestDTO, DeadlineDTO, ReservationDTO, DomiciliationRequestDTO, ResponseDomiAdminDTO)
explanation: pwd has no @JsonIgnore and getPassword() is serialised. DTOs hold whole User objects, so for example any client listing blogs receives the author's bcrypt hash; update-profile returns UserDTO with pwd.
fix: Add @JsonIgnore on pwd/getPassword/code; replace User fields in DTOs with small summary DTOs (id, name).

title: Hard-coded JWT signing key
explanation: The HMAC key is a literal in source code. The repository is public, so anyone can forge a valid token for any e-mail, including the admin.
fix: Load the key from configuration/secret store; rotate it.

title: Hard-coded accountant registration code "abcd"
explanation: Anyone can self-register with role ACCOUNTANT by sending code=abcd, then read all consultation requests and chat with clients.
fix: Create accountants from the admin console only (invitation), never by a shared static code.

title: Admin credentials left in comments
explanation: Commented seeding code contains an admin e-mail and clear-text password. If that account was created this way, the password is public.
fix: Remove the block; change that password if it was ever used.

title: Any client or accountant can delete any account
explanation: DELETE /api/users/delete/{email} deletes whatever e-mail is given; no check that it is the caller's own account (admins can be deleted too).
fix: Delete only the authenticated user's account (or admin-only); compare with SecurityContext.

title: Profile update by path id: overwrite other users and their role
explanation: updateUser(…, id) loads the user from the URL id and forces userRole=CLIENT/ACCOUNTANT. A client can change another user's name, phone and photo, and demote an ADMIN to CLIENT.
fix: Ignore the path id; update the authenticated user; never set the role from this endpoint.

title: Clients can read other clients' domiciliation files
explanation: GET /api/clients/domiciliation-requests/{id} has no ownership check and returns ID-card (CIN) files, contracts and business licences (with file bytes).
fix: Check request.client == authenticated user (or admin).

title: Clients can cancel other clients' requests
explanation: Consultation and domiciliation requests are deleted by id without checking who owns them.
fix: Add an ownership check before delete.

title: Clients can accept/protest contracts of other clients
explanation: acceptContractTermsClient/protestContractTermsClient act on any request id.
fix: Check ownership and the current status before changing it.

title: Any client/accountant can read any chat
explanation: /chat/messages/{id} and /all-chats/{id} return messages of any chat id; messages include the sender User entity (see S03).
fix: Allow only the chat's client and accountant.

title: Accountants can modify or delete anyone's blog posts
explanation: updateBlog/deleteBlog/archiveBlog never check blog.createdBy, so an accountant can edit or delete the admin's posts.
fix: Check authorship (or admin role).

title: Chat service has no authentication; sender id is trusted from the client
explanation: The STOMP endpoint accepts anyone. The userId header decides who 'sent' the message, and anyone can subscribe to /topic/{roomId} to read a conversation.
fix: Authenticate the WebSocket handshake with the JWT; take the sender from the authenticated principal; authorise subscriptions.

title: CORS allows any origin and any header
explanation: Access-Control-Allow-Origin: * on the whole API. Impact is limited because the token is a bearer header, not a cookie.
fix: Use Spring's CorsConfiguration with the real front-end origin(s).

title: No protection against password guessing on login
explanation: No rate limit, lockout or delay on /api/auth/login.
fix: Add rate limiting / progressive delay per account and IP.

title: Upload checks trust the client Content-Type
explanation: Only the declared MIME type is checked; the bytes are never inspected. Files are stored in MongoDB and served back to users.
fix: Check magic bytes / size; store outside the DB; serve with Content-Disposition: attachment.

title: JSON built by string concatenation with untrusted text
explanation: Bodies like "{\"message\":\"" + e.getMessage() + "\"}" break or can be altered when the message contains quotes (it can contain the user's e-mail).
fix: Return a Map/record and let Jackson serialise it.

title: Angular sanitizer bypassed on consultation details
explanation: bypassSecurityTrustHtml(item.details) renders raw HTML typed by the client (self-XSS today; stored XSS if the view is ever reused for other users).
fix: Remove the bypass; Angular's default [innerHTML] sanitising is enough.

title: OAuth client secret was in the properties file (now a placeholder)
explanation: The copy shared privately held a real Google client secret; the public repo uses ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET}. The property is not even used by the code (no oauth2ResourceServer() in the security chain).
fix: Revoke the secret that was shared; remove the unused OAuth properties or wire them properly.

title: Chat content and data written to the browser console
explanation: Messages and API responses are logged in the console of every user.
fix: Remove debug logging from production builds.

title: Optional.get() without check: unknown ids crash with HTTP 500
explanation: findById(...).get() throws NoSuchElementException when the id (or the 'Default' blog category) does not exist; the request fails with 500.
fix: Use orElseThrow(NotFoundException) and map it to 404.

title: String fields compared without null check
explanation: signupRequest.getRole(), getCompanyStatus(), getPaymentMode(), getOldLegalForm(), file.getType() are dereferenced directly; a missing field gives a NullPointerException.
fix: Use enums with @NotNull validation, or "literal".equals(value).

title: Operator-precedence bug in every file-type check
explanation: file != null && (A || B) || C: when file is null the third test still runs and throws NullPointerException; getContentType() may also be null.
fix: Write one helper: file != null && ALLOWED.contains(file.getContentType()).

title: Contract acceptance can crash and poison the scheduler
explanation: If a client accepts before the admin answered, getResponseDomiAdmin() is null (NPE). If paymentMode is null, limitedDate stays null and checkDeadlines() throws NPE every second.
fix: Check the request status before accepting; make paymentMode mandatory.

title: Reminder/overdue flag logic is inconsistent
explanation: emailSent is set true, saved, then set false only in memory (lines 58-60, 67-68, 80, 83). Once 'true' is persisted the overdue branch never runs again for that request; no e-mail is actually sent.
fix: Model reminder state explicitly (lastReminderAt, lastOverdueAt) and send real notifications.

title: Room double-booking: overlap check only matches identical slots
explanation: acceptReservation compares with equals() (same start, same end, same room). 10:00-12:00 and 11:00-13:00 can both be accepted.
fix: Query for overlapping ACCEPTED reservations (start < otherEnd && end > otherStart).

title: Money computed with float
explanation: Prices are float; BigDecimal.valueOf(float) widens to double, so 70.1 becomes 70.0999984741211 before tax and rounding. Also uses the deprecated ROUND_HALF_UP.
fix: Store prices as BigDecimal (or millimes as long); use RoundingMode.HALF_UP.

title: Hard-coded absolute Windows paths of the author's PC
explanation: CSV exports for the recommendation service are written to C:/Users/ouert/Desktop/...; on any other machine the write fails (silently, see R09).
fix: Make the path a configuration property; better, let the Python service read MongoDB directly.

title: Exceptions swallowed with printStackTrace
explanation: Export failures are printed and ignored; the caller reports success.
fix: Log with the logger and propagate or report the failure.

title: Lombok @Builder drops field defaults
explanation: Fields initialised inline (createdAt = now(), lists = new ArrayList<>()) are null when objects are built with the builder, unless @Builder.Default is used. Seeded rooms get createdAt = null.
fix: Add @Builder.Default or initialise in a constructor.

title: Seed data parsed wrongly and re-written at every start
explanation: line.split(",") splits inside the quoted equipment list, so each seeded room keeps only its first equipment. The 6 rooms are overwritten each time the API starts.
fix: Use a CSV parser (OpenCSV is already a dependency) and seed only if empty.

title: Bad-word filter rejects normal business words
explanation: Substring matching on short words ("con", "cul", "pd", "tg") blocks words like contrat, consultation, compte, calcul: exactly the vocabulary of this business.
fix: Match whole words (regex \b...\b) and keep the list in configuration.

title: Uncaught JWT and login exceptions return 500
explanation: An expired or malformed token throws inside the filter (500, not 401). Login only catches BadCredentialsException, not DisabledException/LockedException (archived users).
fix: Catch JwtException in the filter; handle AuthenticationException globally.

title: Possible infinite recursion in toString/hashCode
explanation: @Data/@ToString on the bidirectional Chat <-> Message relation: calling toString() or hashCode() on either recurses until StackOverflowError.
fix: Exclude the back-reference (@ToString.Exclude, @EqualsAndHashCode.Exclude).

title: Front end never releases subscriptions or the WebSocket
explanation: Each visit to the chat opens a new STOMP connection and subscription that is never closed; other components keep subscriptions alive after navigation.
fix: Unsubscribe in ngOnDestroy (takeUntil) and disconnect the STOMP client.

title: Silent failures and broken features
explanation: changePassword returns success when the id does not exist. The front end calls /api/auth/verifyEmail and /password-reset-request, which the API does not implement; resetPassword posts to a URL read from a cookie.
fix: Throw when the user is missing; implement or remove the reset flow.

title: Generic RuntimeException wrapping and malformed error bodies
explanation: Checked exceptions are re-thrown as RuntimeException (500); several error bodies miss their braces and are not valid JSON.
fix: Use a @ControllerAdvice with typed exceptions and a standard error body.

title: Phone-number regex has a broken character class
explanation: [2-5-4-7|9] also accepts '-' and '|' as the first character.
fix: Use ^[2-9]\d{7}$ (or the exact list of Tunisian prefixes).

title: Scheduler reloads all deadlines every second
explanation: @Scheduled(fixedRate = 1000) loads every domiciliation request with a deadline, each with about 10 eager @DBRef objects (files with their bytes, users with photos): 86,400 times a day.
fix: Run daily (cron), query only deadlines in the next 5 days, project only the needed fields.

title: File contents stored inside documents and sent in every list
explanation: byte[] fileData / image are loaded through @DBRef whenever a request, blog, chat or user is read, and serialised as base64 in list responses (e.g. all domiciliation requests with up to 9 files each).
fix: Store files in GridFS/object storage; return metadata + a download URL; exclude bytes from lists.

title: N+1 queries on deadlines
explanation: One findByDeadline() query per deadline in the loop.
fix: Fetch the requests for all deadlines in one query (deadline in [...]).

title: Database calls inside loops
explanation: addReservation reloads the same room for every slot; deleteBlogCategory saves blogs one by one; archiveBlog loads all users and rewrites all of them with saveAll.
fix: Load once outside the loop; use saveAll on the changed items only; use an update query ($pull) for archiveBlog.

title: Full collection scans and in-memory filtering
explanation: validateConsultationRequest loads all chats to find one; clients are filtered in Java; getPackCounts loads every pack with its full user list just to count.
fix: Use derived queries (findByClientAndAccountant, findByUserRoleAndEnabled...) and count queries.

title: Pack embeds full User documents (unbounded growth)
explanation: users is a Set<User> without @DBRef, so whole user documents (photo bytes, password hash) are copied into each pack; the document grows with every subscriber toward MongoDB's 16 MB limit.
fix: Keep only user ids (or a counter) in Pack.

title: Chat history list grows forever and is rewritten on each message
explanation: Sending one message loads the chat with all previous messages (eager @DBRef) and saves the whole array: cost grows with history length.
fix: Do not keep messages inside Chat; query messages by chatId with paging.

title: No pagination on any list endpoint
explanation: All lists (users, requests, blogs, reservations, deadlines) are returned in full.
fix: Use Pageable / Page<T> in repositories and endpoints.

title: God class: DomiAffaireServiceImpl
explanation: Users, files, chats, consultations, domiciliation, packs, blogs, FAQs and reporting all live in one class.
fix: Split by domain (UserService, DomiciliationService, BlogService, ChatService...).

title: Heavy code duplication
location: app/api/src/main/java/com/domiaffaire/api/services/DomiAffaireServiceImpl.java:390-595 (3 near-identical methods), File.builder block x12, auth-user lookup x~35; controllers repeat the same endpoints
explanation: The same code is copied many times: three sendDomiciliationRequest variants, the 'find authenticated user' block, the upload type check (x6), identical blog/chat endpoints in Client/Accountant/User controllers, two branches of updateUser.
fix: Extract helpers (currentUser(), saveFile(), allowedType()), merge controllers.

title: Dead and commented-out code
explanation: 100+ commented lines, unused methods (findAllUsers, uploadFile, findAllFiles, resetUserPassword, generateRefreshToken), unused field tokenBlacklist, unused locals, unused import, unused RestTemplate bean and WebSocket config in the API.
fix: Delete; version control keeps the history.

title: Conditions that are always true
explanation: newFile != null right after new File(); admin != null right after .get(). The 'return null' branches are unreachable.
fix: Remove the dead conditions.

title: Layering bypassed: controllers use repositories and concrete classes
explanation: AuthController calls UserRepository directly; controllers depend on implementations instead of the service interfaces that exist.
fix: Inject the interfaces; keep data access in services.

title: Magic numbers and hard-coded literals
explanation: Token lifetime 10000*60*24 = 4 h (probably meant 24 h); tax rates 0.19 and 0.1; category name 'Default'; status strings 'In Process', 'Quarter'; API URL in environment.ts (seen in step 1).
fix: Named constants, enums and configuration properties.

title: Same domain model duplicated in two services
explanation: User/Chat/Message are defined twice and already differ; a change in one service silently breaks the other.
fix: Share a module, or let only one service own the chat data.

title: Outdated, conflicting or incompatible dependencies
explanation: jjwt 0.9.1 together with jjwt 0.11.5; springfox (does not support Spring Boot 3, plus @EnableWebMvc disables Boot's MVC auto-configuration); android-json in a server; unused webflux/google-api-client; npm peer conflict.
fix: Remove unused libraries, keep one jjwt, replace springfox with springdoc-openapi.

title: Debug output left in code
location: app/api/src/main/java/com/domiaffaire/api/controllers/ClientController.java:184; AccountantController.java:114; UserController.java:40; ReservationServiceImpl.java:127,151; front end: 182 console.log
explanation: System.out.println and console.log used for debugging; the controller lines even call the service twice just to print a size.
fix: Use the logger at debug level; strip console.log in production.

title: Long, deeply nested methods
explanation: Several branches, nested ifs and side effects mixed in one method (status, pack, deadline, notification, document code).
fix: Split into small steps; replace if/else chains on PaymentMode with an enum method (months()).

title: Too many parameters
explanation: sendDomiciliationRequestPMTransfert takes 7 parameters (6 files).
fix: Group the files into one request object.

title: Unclear or misleading text in code
explanation: User-facing message in Tunisian dialect slang; comments in mixed languages; a comment says 'convert nanoseconds to milliseconds' but nothing is converted.
fix: Use clear, consistent messages (i18n) and accurate comments.

title: State changes through HTTP GET
explanation: archive/unarchive, accept/reject reservation and save/unsave blog are GET requests; they can be triggered by prefetching or a simple link.
fix: Use POST/PUT/DELETE for state changes.

title: Almost no automated tests
location: app/api/src/test (2 test classes, about 300 lines for about 6,800 lines of Java)
explanation: None of the bugs above (null handling, ownership, money, scheduling) is covered by a test.
fix: Add service tests for each rule and security tests for each role.

title: Methods with more than 2 data accesses
explanation: 29 methods send 3 to 9 repository calls each instead of one efficient query.

title: Method with more than 7 data accesses
explanation: sendDomiciliationRequestPMTransfert: 1 user lookup + 6 file saves + 1 pack lookup + 1 save = 9.

title: Methods with more than 5 outward calls (fan-out)
explanation: Heuristic count of distinct calls on other objects; includes getters, so it is an upper estimate.

title: Data elements aggregating more than 5 non-primitive elements
explanation: Up to 14 File/User/Pack/Deadline/Response references in one document (enums and dates not counted).

title: Text built by incremental concatenation
explanation: Immutable strings rebuilt in loops instead of using join/builder.

title: Switch statements without default case
explanation: Unknown actions are silently ignored.

title: Method with excessive commented-out code
explanation: Table 1 sets 2 % (3 methods exceed it), pattern 8.115 sets 5 % (1 method); the stricter-consistent count 1 is used.

title: Hard-coded network resource identifiers
explanation: Origins and backend URLs written as literals (localhost:4200/8080/8084).

title: Hard-coded literals used to initialise data
explanation: Seed data and word lists initialised from literals instead of configuration.

title: Layer-skipping call: controller uses repository
explanation: Controller -> repository bypasses the service layer (also CWE-1057 in Performance/Security, counted with S14).

title: Declared exceptions not caught by the caller
explanation: Service methods declared 'throws IOException' are called without catching it; the framework returns a raw 500.

title: User input controls a loop bound
explanation: addReservation loops over a client-supplied list of slots with no size limit (one DB write per slot).

title: Caught security exception not logged
explanation: BadCredentialsException is caught and answered with 401 but never logged, so failed logins leave no trace.

title: Use of an obsolete function
explanation: BigDecimal.ROUND_HALF_UP is deprecated (use RoundingMode.HALF_UP).

title: Query on a field without index (potential)
explanation: No @Indexed on email; counts only once the collection exceeds 500 rows (threshold), so 0 today.
